items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: I’m not going to pay you, Sonny Rollins. I’m not going to pay you until your record costs are paid off.

ctx.x: The fellows that I talked to that were recording in the forties say basically the same thing, that they never made much money off the records, if any.

Well there was a period where it seemed like I was making a ton of publishing money. But we’d never see any actual royalties. Because the publishing money comes from the first record. If you write a song and maybe it’s a song that somebody, it’s not even your song. So they have to pay that person. They can’t hold that money up. Like they can hold the artist’s money up on a record because whatever it cost to make a record they could say well I’m not going to pay you, Sonny Rollins. I’m not going to pay you until…
It must be nice when people from other groups and so forth, record some of your music that you’ve written.
